full_judgment:
9. Mr. MA Mannan Mohan, the learned Deputy Attorney-General with Mr. Md. Sheikh Ensan Uddin and Mr. Md. Osman Gani Khan, the learned Assistant Attorney-Generals appearing on behalf of the State having taken us through the judgment and order under the reference, the FIR, the charge sheet, the deposition of the prosecution witnesses and other materials on record makes his submission supporting the reference and opposing the appeals. He submits that the deceased Tipu has been murdered in a hidden away by the condemned prisoner Zakaria Kabiraj who was introduced with the deceased through his friend Helal, Since deceased was in Japan for 13-14 years, he was a man of sound and rich economy and the condemned prisoner Zakaria Kabiraj being acquainted with the deceased could not check his temptation and before the date of occurrence the condemned prisoner took money from the deceased for purchasing some land at a lowest price but in fact no land was purchased and on the date of occurrence on 14-8-2004 the deceased had gone to accused at Kapasia with Tk. 2,00,000 and he was lastly seen in the company of accused after the magrib prayer and on the following day the dead body of Tipu was found in the guava garden of Gazi Aftab Sheikh, a very adjacent place to the house of father-in-law of the accused. The accused had stayed in the house of his father-in-law Nurul Islam in the night of occurrence and after the occurrence the accused had become puzzled and without informing the members of the family of his father-in-law he left the house leaving his motorcycle and all these facts have been proved by the cogent, credible and reliable evidence of the prosecution witnesses. There appears no explanation from the accused as to the safe departure of the deceased from his company. The circumstantial evidence of this case has been knitted in a manner against the accused that no other hypothesis other than the guilt of the accused can be inferred and the Tribunal considering the unbreakable chain of circumstances rightly found the accused guilty under section 302/34 of the Penal Code. So, the judgment and order of conviction and sentence do not cal1 for interference from this court. The learned Deputy Attorney-General in support of his submission relied upon the case of Anisur Rahman vs State reported in 6 BLD (AD) 79, Billal vs State reported in 52 DLR (AD) 143 and Vola vs State 55 DLR 36. 

 67. In this case the PWs 3, 4, 5, 15 and 26 are the close relations of the accused who are the members of his father-in-law's family. They have given incriminating evidence against the accused. They were cross-examined by the defence extensively but their evidences have not been shaken away in any way for which we can discard their such neat and clean evidence. There was no any such event or suggestion that there was a disgusting relation between the accused and his wife PW 5 and those witnesses were not connected with the father-in-law's family of the accused. So, the incriminating evidence of those witnesses in respect of stay of the accused from the evening of 14-8-2004 till the morning of 15-8-2004 and the movement of the accused for that night, his puzzlement and leaving the house of PW 26 without informing them is very much inculpatory and relevant in this case. In the case of Billal vs State 52 DLR (AD) 143 held in the following ways: 

 69. Now, if we encapsulate the prosecution case as well as the evidence and other materials on record we find that though the victim was not known to the accused before 6-7 months of the date of occurrence but before 6-7 months of the occurrence the deceased was introduced to accused Zakaria Kabiraj through his friend Helal. Thereafter, affinity between the accused and the deceased was developed and though the relationship was started for having treatment of deceased by the accused but ultimately it had reached in purchasing a land at the lowest price by the deceased with the help of the accused and in the afternoon on 14-8-2004 on a definite invitation of the accused, the victim had gone to the accused and the victim was last seen in the company of the accused at Chandpur bazaar and also at Sarker market after the Magrib prayer of the same day. Thereafter with a short gap of 10/11 hours the dead body was found in the guava garden, a adjacent area of the house PW 26, the father-in-law of the accused and the accused had been in the said house of PW 26 at the night of occurrence who had visited the guava garden repeatedly on the false plea to attend natural call but he did not attend to any natural call and after the mid night of the night of occurrence he became very puzzled and hearing the news of the dead body of an unknown man he had left the house of PW 26 leaving his motorcycle and the victim had gone to Zakaria with a cash of Taka 2,00,000 which has been proved by PWs 9, 10 and 17. Thus from the above narrated facts, an unbreakable chain of circumstances has been boosted establishing the involvement of the accused with the murder of the deceased Tipu. The facts of the case has knitted the circumstantial evidence enmeshing the accused with murder of Tipu which is full, jammed and exhaustive having no gap in it that after the last seen of the victim in the company of the accused (accused) he accused was in the touch of the deceased as well as the place of occurrence till his dead body was found. As such it has been proved beyond all reasonable doubt that accused Zakaria had murdered the deceased or abetted in murdering him. So, the accused had rightly been found guilty for the commission of murder of deceased Tipu. But keeping in the view, the decision of the case of 52 DLR (AD) 143 we hold that the accused should have been convicted under sections 302/109 of the Penal Code instead of sections 302/34 of the Penal Code'.
